title: Topics in Cognitive Science
description: Cognitive science is the interdisciplinary study of how minds work. The project of understanding the mind requires tools drawn from fields that include psychology, computer science, philosophy, linguistics, anthropology, behavioral economics, neuroscience, and even the arts. This course is designed for graduate students from all disciplines wishing to understand the fundamentals of cognitive science. It will introduce you to the major tools and theories from these areas as they relate to the study of the mind. This course is the core requirement of the UCSB graduate emphasis in cognitive science, and It serves as a foundation for continued study in the cognitive sciences.

title: The Profession of Academic Philosophy
description: Introduces students to the evolving realities of the profession of academic philosophy. It orients students towards success in the Ph.D. program milestones: the qualifying paper, prospectus development, and completion of the dissertation. It also imparts skills that go beyond graduation, such as preparing a CV, crafting a syllabus, delivering research talks, and writing proposals for grants and fellowships. In the course of covering these topics, the class will also provide a forum for students to reflect on issues in academia more broadly. These include pedagogical innovation, work/life balance, the current state of the discipline, the purposes of the university, and how best to support our diverse undergraduate population.

title: Apprentice Teaching in Philosophy
description: A teaching practicum involving the study and development of effective teaching techniques in philosophy. One meetingper week with instructor and one or more discussion section meetings, and attendance in the lecture of the assigned course are required.

title: Basic Physics
description: Introduction to classical mechanics for students in engineering and the physical sciences. Measurement, units, and foundations of physics; vectors; kinematics; circular motion; forces, mass, and Newton's laws; center of mass; momentum; work and energy; conservation laws; collisions; rotational kinematics.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

title: Basic Physics
description: Rotational dynamics and angular momentum; equilibrium and elasticity; periodic motion including LRC electrical circuits; gravitation; fluid mechanics; temperature; thermal expansion; heat and the first law of thermodynamics; heat conduction; kinetic theory of gases; entropy and the second law; heat engines.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 1 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

title: Basic Physics
description: Mechanical waves, wave interference and normal modes, sound and hearing, electric field, Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.
prerequisites_raw: Physics 2 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B (AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better) and 4A.

title: Basic Physics
description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.
